description: Team Ares Core is formed to tackle NASA's astronaut health monitoring challenge. Our mission is to build a reliable, offline-capable health monitoring interface that helps crew members track vital signs, conduct self-evaluations, and respond quickly to physiological changes during long-duration space missions.
summary:
This is a desktop-based health monitoring software designed for astronauts aboard spacecraft. It simulates real-time biomedical and environmental telemetry, compares readings against aerospace medical thresholds, and provides color-coded alerts with actionable recommendations. The software also includes a 2-minute cognitive reaction test to detect fatigue or cognitive degradation, with results announced via an AI voice assistant and automatically returning to the main dashboard.
The software has a dark "mission-control" aesthetic with cyan accents, a live UTC/GMT clock, and a three-page navigation flow (Dashboard → Cognitive Test → Results).
details: Built with Python, PyQt5, and pyttsx3, CHIRON is a dark-themed, single-window mission-control dashboard engineered to support autonomous crew health and environmental safety during long-duration deep-space missions where Earth communication delays demand onboard diagnostic intelligence. Operating across a modular QStackedWidget architecture, the system continuously tracks nine critical physiological and habitat telemetry streams (such as heart rate, {SpO}, cabin , and radiation) in rolling deque buffers, evaluating them against aerospace thresholds to trigger color-coded alerts and actionable flight-surgeon protocols, while simultaneously offering a timed cognitive reaction test to assess neurological fatigue. By offloading automated voice recommendations to non-blocking QThread background workers, CHIRON ensures zero-latency UI responsiveness under high-stress conditions—ultimately bridging physical biometrics with cognitive acuity to protect astronaut decision-making and establish a scalable blueprint for future hardware-integrated aerospace and extreme-environment tele-health systems.
